**Observations:**
- Affected part: Leaf (upper surface visible)
- Multiple small-to-medium brown/tan lesions scattered across the leaf
- Spots have darker brown perimeters with lighter tan/gray centers
- Some spots show possible yellowish halos
- No white powdery coating, no large necrotic V-shaped lesions, no concentric bullseye rings
- Leaf remains mostly green; lesions distributed across the blade

**Reasoning through candidates:**
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Matches well — small circular lesions with dark-brown perimeters, lighter centers (where pycnidia form), possible yellow halos, scattered distribution
- **Early Blight**: Lesions here lack the distinct concentric ring "bullseye" pattern and are not large dark-brown targets
- **Bacterial Speck**: Spots would be pinpoint-sized (1/16 in.) and very angular; these are larger and rounder
- **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus**: Would show bronzing, downward-cupped leaves, and blurred lesion margins — not seen here

The dark-bordered spots with lighter centers and possible halos on an otherwise green leaf strongly match Septoria Leaf Blotch.
